analysis: The trial succeeded with host validation macro HR@10 of 0.5900, improving over 0.5637 by 0.0263 but remaining 0.0300 below the historical 0.6200. Per-category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.665, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.560, Electronics 0.405, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.730. Electronics remains the weakest category. The result supports retaining reconstruction while adding continuation supervision, although this run alone cannot isolate the auxiliary loss’s causal contribution. Execution completed successfully using 567.86 allocated GPU-seconds; no held-out test results were used.
code_summary: Preserves four independently routed category ensembles. Each combines MultVAE (256 hidden units, 64 latent dimensions, dropout 0.5) with SASRec (50 hidden units, two attention blocks, one head, length 50). MultVAE retains uniform normalized binary-history inputs and multinomial reconstruction plus annealed KL, adding 0.5-weighted full-catalog next-item cross-entropy from randomly sampled chronological prefixes. Singletons receive reconstruction only; prefixes exclude future suffixes, padding is excluded from auxiliary softmax, and repeated targets remain eligible. SASRec retains positive-plus-16-negative cross-entropy. Inference uses unchanged reciprocal-rank fusion: 0.75/(10+r_vae) + 0.25/(10+r_sasrec), with one-based ranks. Checkpoints use validation HR@10 with NDCG@10 tie-breaking; the generated predictor reloads both saved architectures and shares full-history scoring helpers.
